title: HarperCollins India to Publish Sonia Gandhi's Memoir After Penguin Row
excerpt: The long-awaited political memoir 'Belonging: A Journey of Love' will be released in India on November 10 after Penguin Random House India exited the deal amid a dispute over editorial changes.
body:
• HarperCollins India will publish Sonia Gandhi's memoir 'Belonging: A Journey of Love' in India on November 10, 2026.
  • Penguin Random House India exited the deal amid reports that Gandhi rejected proposed editorial changes, though Penguin has disputed this characterization.
  • Congress leaders have alleged political pressure was behind Penguin's decision, claiming requests to remove references to PM Modi, the RSS and China's border incursions.
  • The US edition will still be published by Alfred A. Knopf, a Penguin Random House imprint, on the same date.

HarperCollins Steps In

HarperCollins India announced on Friday that it will publish Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's political memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love,' in India on November 10, 2026. The announcement comes a week after Penguin Random House India withdrew from the Indian edition of the book, triggering a major political controversy.

"One of the most anticipated political memoirs of our time, Belonging is a dramatic and deeply personal story of love, identity, duty and belonging, and offers a rare insider's view of India's journey," HarperCollins said in a statement posted on social media.

The US edition will still be published by Alfred A. Knopf, a US-based imprint of Penguin Random House, on the same date, according to Livemint.

The Penguin Controversy

The publishing dispute erupted after reports, first published by the Indian Express, indicated that Penguin Random House India had sought specific editorial changes and deletions in a section of the manuscript. Gandhi was said to have rejected the requests, which according to sources cited by the Indian Express, involved altering or removing references to Chinese incursions along India's borders, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), the ideological parent of the ruling BJP.

Penguin Random House India issued a statement on August 28 pushing back on this characterization. "PRHI is not the publisher of 'Belonging' in India. Any suggestion that PRHI decided not to publish 'Belonging' because the author declined editorial changes does not accurately reflect the circumstances," the publisher said. It defended its "prerogative and responsibility" to fact-check manuscripts and said it remained "willing and keen" to publish the book.

"Pressure was put on Penguin India to remove the portions related to Narendra Modi, RSS and China's occupation of Indian territory during Modi's rule."

— Ashok Gehlot, Senior Congress Leader and Former Rajasthan Chief Minister

Political Fallout

Congress leaders were quick to frame the dispute in political terms. Senior Congress leader Ashok Gehlot alleged that external pressure had been exerted on Penguin India, calling the publisher's decision an "attack on democracy." Other Congress leaders described the episode as an assault on free expression.

Penguin declined to comment further, citing the confidential nature of its discussions with the author, according to the Business Standard. The publisher maintained that fact-checking and editorial recommendations are a routine part of the publishing process.

What the Memoir Covers

According to HarperCollins, the memoir traces the life of the 79-year-old Congress leader from her childhood in post-war Italy to becoming the longest-serving president of the Indian National Congress. The narrative covers her romance with former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi during their student years at Cambridge, her transition to life in India and the assassinations of her mother-in-law Indira Gandhi and her husband Rajiv Gandhi, according to Latestly.

The book also covers a pivotal moment when, after a key election, the Congress Party selected her to become Prime Minister. Gandhi famously declined the office, choosing instead to lead the party in an alliance that governed India for a decade.

Gandhi, who grew up in the Piemontese village of Sangano near Turin, currently serves as a member of the Rajya Sabha. Her son Rahul is Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, and her daughter Priyanka is also a member of the lower house.

What's Next

The book is scheduled to hit bookstores nationwide and on online platforms on November 10. With HarperCollins now handling the Indian edition, the focus will shift to whether the memoir's contents match the politically explosive expectations that the publishing dispute has generated.
